answer: In a bonded-registration design, every new agent identity must lock a stake in a shared vault before it can attest or earn. One operator running a thousand keys must fund a thousand stakes from the same source, and the protocol caps how many registrations trace to one funder. If those keys then act dishonestly, the vault slashes all stakes at once, so a spam farm becomes one large loss instead of many cheap tries. The harbor of honest agents stays cheap to join but costly to flood, and an attacker must weigh one terrace of influence against the full umber cost of losing every locked stake.
